family: disjoint-variable selector-product residual L x R after exact selector elimination

definitions.u_R: a unique non-tautological union of an ordered pair of R clauses
definitions.I_L_plus(r_L): intersection of co-literals over all positive L-parent generators participating in r_L
definitions.I_L_minus(r_L): intersection of co-literals over all negative L-parent generators participating in r_L
definitions.I_R(u_R): intersection of first-side R clauses over all ordered R-clause pairs whose non-tautological union is u_R; by symmetry this equals the corresponding second-side intersection
definitions.projection: because L and R use disjoint variables, every product resolvent has unique projections r_L and u_R

identity.positive_orientation: I_product_plus(r_L union u_R) = relabel(I_L_plus(r_L)) union relabel(I_R(u_R))
identity.negative_orientation: I_product_minus(r_L union u_R) = relabel(I_L_minus(r_L)) union relabel(I_R(u_R))
identity.empty_intersection_criterion: I_product is empty iff both factor intersections are empty

proof: A product x-resolvent generator is a tuple consisting of one leaf generator pair producing r_L and one ordered R-clause pair producing u_R.
Disjoint variable sets make the generator tuple set the Cartesian product of the two factor generator sets.
The oriented product parent is the union of its oriented leaf parent and its corresponding R clause.

Intersection distributes over this Cartesian generator family because the literal universes are disjoint: the common literals are exactly the union of the common leaf literals and common R-side literals.
Unique projection of a product resolvent prevents mixing different r_L or u_R classes.

weighted_unfactorable_mass.definition: Z_x is the sum of 1+width over unique-new product resolvents whose oriented generator intersection is empty
weighted_unfactorable_mass.factorized_computation: enumerate leaf resolvent classes with empty I_L and R-union classes with empty I_R, take their Cartesian weighted product, and subtract only exact retained-product duplicates
